name: Guardian genius crossword No 272
preamble: A turtle starts on a perimeter cell and moves forward cell by cell. If it lands on an L, it turns 90 degrees anticlockwise; if an R, 90 degrees clockwise; otherwise it continues in the same direction. One word in each clue must be removed before solving; in clue order, these words’ first letters provide an extra instruction. When the turtle exits the grid after making at least one turn, its path has traced what letter?

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former Tory minister breaks parking promises

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister of religion
IOUs are written promises to pay
the superfluous word; its T begins TURTLE in the downs

explanation.surface: A former Conservative minister reneges on promises about parking.
explanation.walkthrough: With Tory removed, the politician is a decoy: minister here means a clergyman, and promises are written IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Previous means coming before in time, as former does in phrases like a former or previous owner.

clue.text: Convict stealing ugly duck returns to prison

indicators.note: a thief takes the loot into his possession, so the word holds the next piece
returning is going back the way you came, so the result is read backwards

blocks.note: an old lag is a habitual convict
a duck is a score of nought in cricket
the superfluous word; its U comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A convict who steals an ugly duckling is sent back to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, hence O. Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaol is the traditional British spelling of jail, a building where prisoners are confined.

clue.text: Stock market index supports risky cryptographic algorithm for cloud

indicators.note: in a down entry, a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the other

blocks.note: SHA is the Secure Hash Algorithm family used in cryptography
the Dow Jones index of the New York Stock Exchange
the superfluous word; its R comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A tech story: a stock index underpins a risky encryption method for cloud computing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloud' looks like cloud computing, which fits the tech surface, but it is a verb meaning to darken.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow something can mean to darken or cast gloom over it, which is what clouds do.

clue.text: In general, during two days, adult tastes drink

indicators.note: the pieces that follow are placed in the middle of the general's name
during means within a span of time, so this piece falls between the two days

blocks.note: Robert E Lee, the Confederate general
MON for Monday and D for day
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
the superfluous word; its T comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, over a couple of days an adult samples a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally', but general is the Confederate commander Robert E Lee, and In tells the solver to put pieces inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a sweet lemon-flavoured soft drink, so it is one particular drink.

clue.text: Look, Arizona backs government's drug laws

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for government
AZ is the postal code for the US state of Arizona
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the superfluous word; its L comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Behold: Arizona supports the federal government's drug laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' sounds like a speaker's opening word; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze is to look steadily and at length, so it is a particular way of looking.

clue.text: Comedian's best ever

blocks.note: taken as written
the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop
the superfluous word; its E comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Praise for the greatest comedian of all time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comedian's best ever' reads as a review; remove ever and the 's supplies its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a funny person a scream is informal praise meaning they are hilarious, a natural comedian.

clue.text: British doctor hates saving toy soldiers' lives

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece is held within the other
to doctor is to tamper with or falsify, so the combined letters are rearranged

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
taken as written
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the superfluous word; its T starts the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A British doctor who loathes war games nonetheless rescues a child's toy soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove 'toy' first. 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the anagram signal, acting on the word hates once it has saved the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe is to be alive, so someone who breathes still lives; both verbs describe existing.

clue.text: Relative tries dancing foxtrot with son

indicators.note: dancers move about and change places, so these letters swap positions

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son
the superfluous word; its F begins FACES

explanation.surface: A family member attempts a foxtrot with her son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxtrot' fits the dancing so well it seems essential, but it is the extra word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a female sibling, one of a person's closest family relations.

clue.text: Old church employs a rector and old bishop

indicators.note: an employer takes staff in, so the outer letters take the next ones inside them

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
CH is the usual abbreviation for church
taken as written
R is an abbreviation for rector
the superfluous word, the second of the two; its O comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: An ancient church takes on a rector and an elderly bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two olds; the second is the extra word, so bishop alone is the definition and the first Old starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch is a senior bishop in the Eastern Orthodox churches, ranking above a metropolitan in some traditions.

clue.text: Ground beef, eggs and slice of lamb

indicators.note: a slice is a small cut taken from the front, so only the word's opening letter is kept

blocks.note: ova are egg cells, the Latin plural of ovum
the opening letter
the superfluous word; its B begins the instruction's second word

explanation.surface: A recipe list: minced beef, eggs and a slice of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like minced, describing the beef, but once beef is removed it is the definition: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval is a famous Test cricket venue in Kennington, south London, so it is a sports ground.

clue.text: Found smashing Easter service taken by theologian - it's all about love

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so the word's letters are put back together differently
the whole jumbled group goes around the next piece, surrounding it
to be taken by someone is to be held by them, so the outer letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the superfluous word; its E comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A wonderful Easter service led by a theologian whose message is all about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise for the service; it is the anagram signal. Love as zero comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to find it, so the past tense discovered matches found in the sense of came upon.

clue.text: Perhaps Don Juan's retiring over other genteel ladies initially giving chase

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the word is read backwards in this across entry
initially points at the opening letter of each of the two words just before it
the outer word spreads over the inserted letters, covering them on both sides

blocks.note: a wolf is a predatory womaniser, of whom Don Juan is the classic example
the opening letter
the opening letter
the superfluous word; its G begins BEGIN's last letters run

explanation.surface: A notorious seducer, now in retirement, still pursues refined ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Juan stands for a wolf, a womaniser; turned round that is FLOW, which goes over O and L from other ladies, splitting as F-OL-LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone is to go after them, which is what giving chase or chasing means.

clue.text: Ring back to buy single ash tree

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end in this down entry
buying something brings it into your possession, so the word takes the next piece inside

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the Roman numeral one
the superfluous word; its A comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Phone back to order a lone ash tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ash tree' seems a single species, but ash is the extra word and tree alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a small flowering tree or shrub with scented purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Time after time he's describing iceberg's mass in geological units

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so these letters encircle the next one
after sends the first-named piece second, placing it behind the later one

blocks.note: an era is a long period of time
T is the abbreviation for time in physics
taken as written, without the apostrophe
M is the symbol for mass
the superfluous word; its I comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Time and again, someone describes an iceberg's mass in terms of geological units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' reads as 'repeatedly', but it is two different words for time, with the first placed after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An erathem is the body of rock laid down during a geological era, a unit of the stratigraphic scale.

clue.text: Poem about unseating King Charles has international leaders shocked

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so each word gives only its opening letter
something shocked is jolted out of place, so the gathered letters are reordered

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
the opening letters of these two words
the superfluous word; its C comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A poem about deposing King Charles leaves world leaders aghast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Charles' reads as one figure; Charles is the extra word, and King gives only its K.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese form of poem in three lines of five, seven and five syllables.

clue.text: Small boy leaving tiny particle to pick nose

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are gone, so those letters disappear from the longer word

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an electron is a subatomic particle
Ron is a boy's name
the superfluous word; its N completes BEGIN

explanation.surface: A little boy abandons his tiny particle so he can pick his nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Delete 'nose' and the schoolboy joke vanishes, leaving pick as a verb meaning choose.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to choose, which is what to pick means when you pick a team or a winner.

clue.text: Equated new moped with electric car

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
joins the two words that are mixed together
taken as written
the superfluous word; its E comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A review that weighs up a new moped against an electric car.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare one thing with another is to liken or set them side by side as equivalent.

clue.text: Writing piece about winning formula?

indicators.note: about can mean moved around or in disorder, so the word's letters are turned about

blocks.note: writing is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic
taken as written
the superfluous word; its W begins WITH

explanation.surface: An essay about the formula for success.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a recipe is a formula only in a looser, kitchen sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe sets out ingredients and method to produce a dish, much as a formula sets out components for a result.

clue.text: Clutching bible, sinner's happy to be raised up

indicators.note: clutching means gripping tightly in your hands, so the word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: elated means joyful
EV, short for evangel, a gospel book
the superfluous word; its S comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A repentant sinner, holding a bible, is glad to be lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: The bible gives EV, a loose abbreviation for evangel or gospel; ELATED clutches it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means lifted to a higher position, which is to be raised up.

clue.text: Essentially sent one's newest grades to set of nine

indicators.note: the essence of something is at its heart, so only each word's central letters are kept

blocks.note: the central two letters
the central two letters, ignoring the apostrophe
the central two letters
the superfluous word; its N begins NORTH

explanation.surface: Someone has sent their latest marks to a group of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead, from the Greek for nine, is a group of nine, such as the nine gods of Heliopolis.

clue.text: Example of square enclosure holding back infected rodents

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so that word is read from its end
to hold something is to have it within your grasp, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: S taken as a short form of square, as in an address
a pen is an enclosure for animals
mice are small rodents
the superfluous word; its I comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A laboratory sample: a square cage of infected rats and mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infected' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the extra word to discard; 'back' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single sample or instance taken as typical of its kind, which is an example.

clue.text: Instruments playing in soap opera

indicators.note: letters at play move around freely, so these are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the superfluous word; its O comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Musical instruments heard in a television soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap opera' reads as one phrase; opera is the extra word, leaving IN SOAP as the letters to play with.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano is a keyboard instrument whose strings are struck by felt hammers.

clue.text: Thomas Hardy's partner gets award

blocks.note: first meaning: Stan ..., comedy partner of Oliver Hardy in ... and Hardy
second meaning: a wreath of bay leaves given as an honour
the superfluous word; its T begins THE

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thomas' points to the novelist Thomas Hardy; remove it and Hardy is Oliver Hardy, the film comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the double act, and a laurel wreath has honoured victors since ancient Greece.

clue.text: Most recent news of Los Angeles robber on trial

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles
a test is a trial
the superfluous word; its R comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Breaking news of a Los Angeles robber's court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On trial' suggests a courtroom; remove robber and 'on' just places LA above TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the most up-to-date information, as in 'have you heard the latest?'

clue.text: Even literature's inspiring Australian workers' honest collective

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer word draws the others inside

blocks.note: on a par means even or level
lit is the short form of literature
A is an abbreviation for Australian
men in the sense of a workforce
the superfluous word; its H comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: Even literature celebrates the honest collective spirit of Australian workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' collective' suggests a trade union. Parliament is also the collective noun for a group of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a collective assembly of representatives, and the word is also a collective noun for owls.

clue.text: Floor covering part of mansion I like returning to

indicators.note: the answer is only a portion of the words that follow, lying across them
returning means coming back the other way, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of mansion, the I and the start of like
the superfluous word; its T comes next in the hidden instruction

explanation.surface: A homeowner fancies a floor covering for part of the mansion they come home to.
explanation.definitionFit: Lino, short for linoleum, is a hard-wearing sheet material laid on floors.

clue.text: I ask you, trace victim of attack by ear

indicators.note: judging by ear means going on how the words are heard, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: prey is a creature attacked by a predator
the superfluous word; its T begins TURTLE

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help tracing the victim of an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I ask you' looks like a frustrated aside, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pray is an old-fashioned polite formula for asking, as in 'pray tell', meaning please or I beg you.

clue.text: Father finally reading the hymn sheet

indicators.note: finally points at the end, so each of the next words gives its closing letter

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
the closing letter
the closing letter
the superfluous word; its H ends the instruction, FACES NORTH

explanation.surface: Dad at last sings from the hymn sheet with everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading from the same hymn sheet' is an idiom for agreeing; hymn is the extra word, leaving sheet as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is one sheet of paper in a book or document, so the words are interchangeable.

clue.text: Black cat hunting as Tigger might do?

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat
the superfluous word; its H continues the instruction's word THE... sequence

explanation.surface: A black cat on the prowl, behaving like Tigger from Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.walkthrough: Tigger, the tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh, is famous for bouncing on his springy tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger sings that bouncing is what tiggers do best, so the verb names his trademark action.

clue.text: In England, is a greenhouse essential? No way!

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follows, spanning several of them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of England through the start of greenhouse
the superfluous word; its E ends the instruction's word THE

explanation.surface: Is a greenhouse really essential in England? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' looks like a middle-letters signal, but it is the extra word; 'In' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an emphatic refusal to accept a claim, which is exactly what it is to disagree.
